what_was_done: The arithmetic part is fixed and pinned. _parentheses_balance closes '$((id)|(id))', the same in double quotes, '$((a)&&(b))' and '$((echo PWNED)|(cat))', and '$(( (1+2)*3 ))' and '$(((1+2)))' stay judgeable. I mutated it away in a scratch copy and test_shell and test_decision_pairing both failed. Outside double quotes the ${...} part is fixed too. "${y:-'}'$(id)}" and '${(e):-\$\(id\)}' are opaque, and reverting _parameter_plain fails test_substitution_beside_arithmetic_in_one_word_is_opaque. But inside double quotes the plain-text rule is never applied. _read_word's double-quote loop checks only '$(', '$((' and backticks. It ends the quoted string at the first '"', even when that '"' opens a quote nested inside ${...}, which sh, bash, dash and zsh all honour. So a quote inside the span still hides its real end, and the rest reads as an unclosed single quote. Three forms parse as one non-opaque vsdd call: 'vsdd survey "${x:-"'"}"$(id)''' runs id under /bin/sh, bash 3.2, bash 5.3, dash and zsh; 'vsdd survey "${x:-'"'}"$(id)''' runs it under sh and both bashes; and the finding's own zsh form in double quotes, 'vsdd survey "${(e):-\$(id)}"', runs it in zsh. A double-quoted setter also plants code that a plain-looking reader then runs. 'vsdd survey "${x:=\$(id)}${x@P}"' runs id under bash 5.3. 'vsdd survey "${x:=a[\$(id)]}" ${!x}' and the same with '$((x))' run it under sh and both bashes. Through the runner, an agent's call in each of the first four forms got the caller marker, permissionDecision 'allow' and updatedInput. No test covers ${...} inside double quotes. To fix: in the double-quote branch of _read_word, on '${', apply _parameter_plain to the text up to the first '}'. With no '}', or with inner text that is not plain, count it as a substitution. Add these to test_shell.py as opaque: 'vsdd survey "${x:-"'"}"$(id)''', 'vsdd survey "${x:-'"'}"$(id)''', 'vsdd survey "${(e):-\$(id)}"' and 'vsdd survey "${x:=\$(id)}"'. Keep 'vsdd survey "${x:-a b}"' judgeable. Add the first form to the agent cases of test_decision_pairing. A scratch sketch of this change closed every probe and kept all 130 tests under tests/hooks passing.

The bracket part is fixed and pinned. With the bracket-expression branch gone, '[ ; id ; ]', '[;id;]', '[ && id ]' and 'a[b|id]' split into segments. '[$(id)]', '[`id`]', '$[$(id)]' and "$['$(id)']" are opaque, and 'a[bc]' stays a judgeable glob. Restoring the branch in a scratch copy failed test_brackets_split_or_are_opaque and test_decision_pairing. Removing the '$[' flag failed the "$['$(id)']" case. But '$[' counts as a substitution only outside double quotes. The double-quote loop of _read_word does not check '$[', and an escaped '\$' hides the substitution from its character scan. So 'vsdd survey "$[a[\$(id)]]"' parses as one non-opaque vsdd segment. It runs id under macOS /bin/sh and /bin/bash 3.2, which expand the array subscript a second time; 'printf' of the command into a file and running it printed PWNED under both. Through the runner, an agent's call got the caller marker, permissionDecision 'allow' and updatedInput. The '$((' form of the same trick, '"$((a[\$(id)]))"', is already opaque because _arithmetic_harmless rejects it. To fix: in the double-quote branch, count a '$[' as a substitution, as the unquoted branch does. Add 'vsdd survey "$[a[\$(id)]]"' to test_brackets_split_or_are_opaque and to the agent cases of test_decision_pairing.
